_comment: Fragment 35 — D-82, the lane model cannot enforce itself; G69 opened. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-82 — D-75 Cannot Enforce Itself
nodes.description: D-75 assigns three lanes and forbids crossing them, but nothing in the repository enforces that. Verified 2026-08-21: no CODEOWNERS at any path, no path-scoped rules, no husky or pre-commit config, zero installed git hooks with the default hooks path, and CI triggering on push and pull_request, which runs after a commit lands. The only control is prose in the shared core.
nodes.rationale: Does not weaken D-75; it removes an overread of it. Four crossings by agents that had already read the rules are on record, two of them by Lane A on the day the lanes were written. CI verifies and cannot prevent.

nodes.label: Every Enforcement Surface Belongs to Lane C
nodes.description: CODEOWNERS lives in .github, a pre-commit hook is build tooling, and a path check would live in scripts/checks. All three are Lane C's surface under D-75. Lane A can therefore specify enforcement and can never apply it, so the first real control must come from Lane C or from the Chief Editor.
nodes.rationale: A property of the model as designed rather than an oversight. It means D-75 is a duty each agent accepts, not a guardrail that holds when one declines.

nodes.label: The Lane Model Is Weakest Where a Codebase Already Exists
nodes.description: In a repository without the implementation, the absence of the artifact is itself a brake. In a project that already has code, a Lane C specification reads as a change request against working code: complete, actionable, and executable by whichever agent opens it.
nodes.rationale: Recorded because the natural assumption runs the other way, that a mature repository is the safer case. The consequence is that every Lane C specification carries an owning-lane banner and an explicit stop line in the artifact itself, not only in the rule file read at session start.

nodes.label: G69 — No Mechanism Enforces the Lane Boundaries
nodes.description: Open gap for the missing control. Candidate mechanisms are CODEOWNERS, a pre-commit path check, or a scripts/checks path rule, each of which sits on Lane C's surface. Specified, not applied.
nodes.rationale: Opened rather than solved, because solving it from Lane A would itself be the crossing the gap describes.
